# 13 — Final report: the closure memory time in the fc3-parametrised rate class (AlN, 300 K)

**Dates:** opened 5 October 2026; interrupted by the loss of drive D: (09, item 9); resumed and completed
10 October 2026. Definitions and declared choices: `02-assumptions.md`. Experiments E1–E18: `07-experiments.md`.
Negative results and bugs: `09-failed-approaches.md`. Independent review: `review/`.

## 0. Declared class (every statement below is about this class)
* **Rates generated by force constants:** g_alpha = W_alpha |Phi_alpha(fc3)|^2 on the fixed AlN three-phonon event set
  of the memory-gap campaign (5x5x3 mesh, Gaussian sigma = 0.1 THz, 300 K; 7x7x5 for the local analysis), with fc2,
  phonons, Bose factors and smearing fixed. The unknown is fc3 in the 7,752-dimensional space of P6_3mc-symmetric,
  permutation-symmetric, sum-rule-satisfying third-order force constants of the 3x3x2 supercell (456 symmetry-
  distinct cluster orbits). Selection-rule zeros are built in.
* **Data:** all 117 mode-orbit lifetimes (r = diag C) within ±10 %, kappa_xx and kappa_zz within ±1 %.
* **Plausibility of fc3 changes** (the class is useless without one, E6–E7): Frobenius bound; uniform per-cluster
  bound eps; or the calibrated per-cluster bound eps_o = max(k delta_o, 0.5 %), delta_o the observed difference
  between two independent first-principles workflows (E13), k = 1, 2.
* All AlN numbers are numbers of these discretised operators on coarse meshes, not converged AlN values.

## 1. Answer to the decision question of paper 1
**The amplitude structure removes the orders-of-magnitude gap of the free-rate class, but at the precision with which
first-principles fc3 are actually known, static transport data do not pin tau_mem to better than a factor of about
two.**
* Free rates (memory-gap campaign): witnesses 10^2–10^5 x the reference.
* fc3 class, Frobenius bound ~10 % (E10): 14 x (x) and 624 x (z) — but only by rewriting single long-range cluster
  orbits by factors up to 43; not a plausible fc3.
* Uniform per-cluster bound (E15–E16): eps = 5 %: [0.88, 1.17] (x), [0.86, 1.23] (z); eps = 10 %: [0.84, 1.31],
  [0.81, 1.37]; eps = 20 %: [0.79, 1.62], [0.76, 1.65] x the reference.
* **Calibrated bound (E17–E18):** k = 1 (each cluster orbit within the observed inter-workflow difference):
  tau_x in [23.9, 80.3] ps = [0.70, 2.35] x, tau_z in [18.8, 59.0] ps = [0.68, 2.15] x; k = 2: [0.64, 3.72] and
  [0.61, 5.96]. The k = 1 witnesses lie 2.1–2.2 % (Frobenius) from the reference fc3 — closer than the second
  workflow itself (2.36 %) — and fit the data better than it does.
* **Mechanism:** in every calibrated witness the on-site and nearest-neighbour constants (99.1 % of ||fc3||^2) move by
  less than 0.7 %; the memory is carried by the long-range constants beyond 3.2 A (0.19 % of ||fc3||^2), on which the
  two workflows disagree by order one.
* **What a real second workflow does** (E13): replacing the phono3py fc3 by the ALAMODE one moves single event rates by
  factors 0.011–43 (0.1–99.9 % quantiles) and lifetimes by up to 18 %, but tau_mem by only −0.75 % (x) and +1.7 % (z).
  So the second workflow happens to lie near the reference memory; the data do not force this.
* **Lower end:** identified as in the free class. Rigorous floor tau >= (1 − dK) tau_CS = 19.00 ps (x), 15.36 ps (z);
  every minimiser found lies within 4–55 % of it (calibrated k = 2: within 15 % and 9 %).
* **Mesh (E14):** at 7x7x5 the first-order data-preserving slope of log tau is mesh-stable in the full space and the
  5 A subspace; in the 3.5 A subspace (218 parameters) the 287 static data have full column rank: the short-range
  fc3 is locally identified and tau has no first-order freedom. The residual freedom therefore lives in the
  long-range constants — consistent with the mechanism above.

## 2. Statements and status
**S1 (fc3 route reproduces the reference) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED.** W pp reproduces the memory-gap rates to
1.3e-15 (5x5x3) and 1.4e-15 (7x7x5); kappa and tau identical (E1). Independent amplitude engine agrees with
phono3py's Rust kernels to 6.5e-12 relative on all allowed events (E2).

**S2 (local controllability) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED.** At 5x5x3 the rate Jacobian has rank 2,113 = number of
independent block rates: every block rate can be moved independently, at first order, by a symmetric fc3 change
(E6). The 335 selection-rule orbits stay zero for every symmetric fc3.

**S3 (rigorous statements).** (a) tau >= K/|b|^2 >= (1 − dK) tau_CS for any admissible rates — PROVED (memory-gap
P4(a), audited there). (b) Frobenius-ball ceiling tau <= 1/lambda_min(C(g_low(rho))) — PROVED (memory-gap P7 with
per-amplitude floors |Phi| >= |Phi0| − ||G_m|| rho |c0|); vacuous from rho = 0.5 % on (E7). No rigorous upper bound
is available for the per-cluster or calibrated classes: amplitudes can be silenced inside them (rate ratios 1e-4 at
eps = 10 %), so per-event floors are void. All quoted maxima are inner bounds.

**S4 (Frobenius class) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED (inner bounds).** Witnesses 481.45 ps (x, eps 9.7 %) and
17,121 ps (z, eps 9.6 %) with all data held; verified by phono3py amplitudes, dense eigendecomposition and CG (E12).

**S5 (uniform per-cluster class) — NUMERICALLY SUPPORTED (inner bounds; multistart).** Table of section 1; four
starts for each eps = 10 % maximum, including the clipped Frobenius witness direction, agree within 2.6 % (x) and
0.5 % (z) (E16). This is evidence against a hidden large-tau branch near these points, not a global certificate.

**S6 (calibration) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED for the mapping; the interpretation is a declared modelling choice.**
The ALAMODE tensor maps into the symmetric space to 5e-14 and satisfies the sum rule to 7e-13 after folding; two
mappings differing by a crystal symmetry agree to 1.2e-16 (E13, 09 item 12). delta_o is ONE inter-workflow
difference, not a statistical uncertainty; the third Olympics workflow (ShengBTE) was not mapped.

**S7 (calibrated class) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED (explicit witnesses, inner bounds).** Values of section 1; each
witness verified by the phono3py route (tau to <= 0.03 %, eig = CG), every per-orbit bound active at ratio 0.999,
degeneracy-averaged lifetimes within 9.98 % (E17–E18).

**S8 (7x7x5 local identifiability of short-range fc3) — NUMERICALLY DEMONSTRATED at first order** (rank 218/218,
smallest singular value 0.118; E14). Local, at the reference only; no 7x7x5 optimisation was run.

**S9 (sensitivity, task 2) — NUMERICAL OBSERVATIONS** (E3–E5): make_r0_average changes tau by 3–10 % and single
event rates by factors 0.02–76; dropping the sum rule in a truncation changes single lifetimes by factors up to 4;
random symmetric perturbations of 1 % already move single lifetimes by 10–47 %, and none of 5–20 % is data-consistent.

## 3. Fragile points and scope
1. All maxima and minima are local; nothing excludes larger tau inside the per-cluster or calibrated classes.
2. The calibration rests on one pair of workflows; the long-range reference constants are themselves products of a
   finite-displacement fit in a 3x3x2 supercell and may be noise-dominated. A larger or different spread would move
   the calibrated range; k = 1 and k = 2 bracket this choice only crudely.
3. fc2 fixed: harmonic uncertainty (the workflows also differ in fc2 and lattice constants) is not propagated.
4. Coarse meshes (5x5x3 for every optimisation). The 7x7x5 reference memory is already 52.6 / 50.6 ps; the
   statements are about ratios at fixed discretisation.
5. Data at one temperature only; the memory-gap campaign showed that large-tau witnesses are observable in kappa(T)
   and in K(z) at finite frequency. Those observables were not added as constraints here.
6. Orbit-average versus block-average conventions differ by up to 6e-4 in kappa ratios for some witnesses (E15, E17);
   the constraints were imposed in the gauge-invariant block convention.

## 4. Conclusion for paper 1
The free-rate memory gap is an artefact of ignoring the amplitude structure: once rates come from symmetric force
constants and the dominant clusters are held to first-principles precision, the gap shrinks from 10^2–10^5 to a factor
of order two. It does not vanish, because the memory time is controlled by the small long-range anharmonic constants,
which neither the static 300 K data nor two independent workflows determine. A conserving closure for AlN can
therefore take tau_mem from first principles only together with a stated fc3-precision model; quoting tau_mem
without such a model overstates what is known. The natural sharpening is (i) a third workflow and a convergence study
of the long-range constants, (ii) adding kappa(T) and finite-frequency response as data, and (iii) a finer mesh.

## 5. Reproduction (C: scripts, results under results/m553)
```
<phono3py env> -B p3_events.py --mesh 5 5 3 --events events_m553_s0.1.npz --outdir <dir> --static     # E1
<phono3py env> -B basis_p3.py <dir>; <research env> -B linearize.py ...; orbit_scaling.py <dir>       # E6, E8
<research env> -B t3_batch.py / t3_batch_min.py <events> <dir> <dir>/t3_orb 4                          # E15
<research env> -B t3_multistart.py <events> <dir> <dir>/t3_ms 3 <witness_x_y> <witness_z_y>            # E16
<phono3py env> -B alamode_compare.py <cubic xml> <dir> <dir>/alamode [mirror|inversion]                # E13
<research env> -B alamode_transport.py <events> <dir> <dir>/alamode/pp_alm_r01_alamode.npz <out>       # E13
<research env> -B orbit_scaling.py <dir> --eps <dir>/alamode/alamode_orbits.npz <k> 0.005 cal<k>       # E17-18
<research env> -B t3_calibrated.py <events> <dir> <dir>/t3_cal 4 <dir>/alamode/alamode_orbits.npz <k>
<research env> -B witness_verify.py build|check ...                                                    # E12, E15-18
<research env> -B local_analysis.py <events_m775> <dir_m775> 5.0 3.5                                   # E14 (D: scripts)
```
Inputs hash-checked at every phono3py run (aln_common.verify_inputs). Large arrays stay outside the repository.
